newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees tax revenues rising 10 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees tax revenues rising 10 pct in 1997.

text.p: Mexican tax revenues are seen rising 10 percent in 1997 over levels collected in 1996, Deputy Finance Minister Tomas Ruiz Gonzalez said.
"For 1997, we are estimating a growth of tax revenues of around 10 percent in real terms over the 1996 base," Ruiz told reporters here in this western Mexican city.
The government projects a 15 percent increase in the consumer price index this year, though most economic analysts expect it will be about 18 percent in 1997.
Ruiz said in the first half of last year revenues dropped more than 14 percent compared to the first half of 1995 but then collection reverted the negative tendency in the second half of 1996.

"However, in the second half this tendency reversed and we have been having positive growth rates of around seven and eight percent (since)...federal government incomes for 1996 were around 400 billion pesos," he added.
Ruiz said the expected increase in tax revenues this year would come through more vigorous investigations into non-tax paying companies and Mexicans.
